claims.text: OpenAI introduced the Codex app on 2026-02-02 as a workspace for managing multiple coding agents and long-running parallel work.
OpenAI introduced GPT-5.3-Codex on 2026-02-05 for coding plus longer-running research, tool use, and complex execution tasks.
The GPT-5.3-Codex System Card was published on 2026-02-05 and applies OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework cybersecurity evaluation to the model.
OpenAI introduced GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark on 2026-02-12 as a research-preview model designed for realtime coding interaction.
Claims such as GPT-5.3-Codex being 25% faster and Codex-Spark exceeding 1,000 tokens/s on Cerebras hardware are vendor-reported performance claims.

claims.text: vLLM v0.16.0 was published on 2026-02-25; its release notes state that the branch was cut on 2026-02-08.
v0.16.0 added a WebSocket-based Realtime API with streaming-audio/Voxtral realtime support, Responses API improvements, tool-calling fixes, unified parallel drafting, and major XPU changes.
The release reports 30.8% end-to-end throughput improvement and 31.8% TPOT improvement for async scheduling plus pipeline parallelism; these are project-reported measurements.
v0.15.1 was published on 2026-02-04 and serves as earlier-month context, but v0.16.0 carries the stronger February systems signal.

limitations.text: The v0.16.0 branch-cut date means it cannot be used as evidence that every late-February model change was already integrated.
Performance figures are project release-note measurements and are not independently reproduced.
The series groups one patch and one major release; architecture should center v0.16.0.
